units.text: EXT. GENERAL STORE PORCH - MORNING
A dusty main street, a hitching rail, a water trough.
Quiet.
A wind chime of old spoons clinks.

SILAS CROWE, fifties, black hat, graying mustache, a stranger who sits on a barrel with a tin cup of coffee, looks up as BESSIE MARSH, forties, the store owner, sweeps the boards by the door, and LITTLE JOE TALLCHIEF, twelve, rolls a hoop down the street with a stick, and REV. ABERNATHY, sixty, a preacher in a rusty black coat, steps out of the church across the way and shades his eyes, all four of them noticing at the same instant the cloud of dust rising far out on the plains.
Riders.
units.name: BESSIE

units.text: Four of them.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: How can you tell?
units.name: LITTLE JOE

units.text: Four plumes. Hush.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Mrs. Marsh, is that the Dalton boys?
units.name: REV. ABERNATHY

units.text: God help us if it is.
units.name: BESSIE

units.text: Silas stands, sets down his cup, and unbuttons his coat.
Bessie leans the broom against the wall.
Little Joe edges toward the porch steps.
Rev. Abernathy crosses the road with surprising speed, his Bible clutched to his chest.
Silas Crowe. I know you from somewhere.
units.name: REV. ABERNATHY

units.text: Never been here, Reverend.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Springfield, 'seventy-eight. The tent revival.
units.name: REV. ABERNATHY

units.text: You must be thinking of another man.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: He's thinking of the man on the wanted poster in my window.
units.name: BESSIE

units.text: Mrs. Marsh, you're sharper than your broom.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Mr. Crowe, are you an outlaw?
units.name: LITTLE JOE

units.text: I'm a retired one.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: The dust cloud grows.
The riders become shapes, then men.
Their hats are low.
Bessie and the Reverend both step back, and Little Joe slips behind the barrel, and Silas Crowe, still smiling, takes off his hat and sets it on the rail.
Ma'am, a cup of that coffee wouldn't hurt.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: You expecting company?
units.name: BESSIE

units.text: I expect they'll want to talk.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: She pours.
He drinks.
The riders pull up at the hitching rail.
The lead one tips his hat, sees Silas, and lets out a long breath.
Morning, boys.
units.name: SILAS
